result.title: On Grokking and the Dynamics of Generalization
result.summary: We extend the signal-channel theory of grokking introduced by Litman and Guo by relating training dissipation and evaluation transfer to population risk. For preconditioned gradient flows with time-dependent kernels, we distinguish two sources of limited evaluation visibility, namely small cumulative dissipation and weak transfer. We obtain quantitative bounds for task visibility and establish their stability under signal filtering and changes of evaluation distribution. We describe how task directions enter the effective signal channel through spectral activation or transport. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the transferred signal to decrease squared population risk and derive classification error bounds under margin assumptions. These results yield sufficient conditions for the same training trajectory to generalize under one evaluation distribution while failing under another. We show that differences in spectral learning rates can produce arbitrarily long delays between low training loss and low population risk. By relating classification accuracy to the distribution of margin crossing times, we construct a family of gradient flows in which the generalization delay tends to infinity, while both the duration of the transition from zero to full accuracy and the corresponding variation of population risk tend to zero. These phenomena occur without feature evolution during training. Finally, we prove that the occurrence and timing of generalization cannot generally be inferred from training dynamics alone, but depend on the geometry of evaluation transfer and its relation to the target.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 signal-channel 理论框架下研究 grokking，将训练耗散与评估转移同 population risk 联系起来，给出任务可见性、分类误差与泛化延迟的定量界，并构造出泛化延迟趋于无穷而训练损失早已降低的梯度流族。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心结论「泛化何时发生无法仅由训练动态推断，而取决于评估转移几何与目标的关系」，可能为 LVR 中区分训练损失下降与 latent 内容是否真正被使用、以及贡献分配与评价设计提供概念线索，需核查这种抽象结论可否迁移到多模态推理场景。
